revision: Homepage follows next event; mode changes composition and restrained accent. Increase character through type and project evidence.

prompts.prompt:
Generate a high-fidelity desktop website homepage UI concept for HackJudge. One complete straight-on wide desktop viewport, 1440 by 1000 style proportions, no device frame, no perspective. This is the actual platform HOMEPAGE, opening on the NEXT scheduled event, not an all-events directory or an interior event detail page. Header shared across modes: bold HackJudge wordmark, Events, Projects, right Sign in. Discreet concept label outside app content "Homepage concept · Sample projects". Shared platform identity: chalk white #FAFAF7 main canvas, deep ink #19222B, crisp dark type, purposeful 8px corners, fine strong rules, pleasing spacious content, bold condensed grotesk event title, clean normal sans body. More distinctive and lively than a sterile blue SaaS dashboard, but still unequivocally a technical competition platform. No big rounded card soup, no generic SaaS analytics dashboard, no decorative abstract project art, no biotech green, no gradients, no excessive tiny uppercase labels, no fake customers/testimonials, no enormous marketing slogans. Strong typographic hierarchy and deliberate asymmetry. Make sample project interfaces and prototypes the visually interesting content, with clear descriptions and team information. Sample project names Voltify (community energy demand forecasting), AgriSense (field sensors and crop insights), MedSync (care coordination), LinguaLink (real-time local-service translation). Illustrative project media must look like plausible prototype screens, electronics or actual work, with small "Sample project" labels; never invent official assets or claims. HEADER and a recognizable compact UPCOMING EVENT strip stay consistent across modes. A secondary narrow "On the calendar" section shows Community showcase / Oct 25 / Demo Day and Code & Tell / Nov 9 with "All events" link; keep this secondary, not the main feature. Event descriptions and previews dominate. Show enough of the second section to demonstrate full homepage layout. This is primarily used during competitions. Current state is upcoming, so no active voting/scoring buttons or fake saved results. Clear first action is "View event", with secondary "Explore projects". Use color as localized accents and panels, never full-screen background brand flooding. Sharply composed, product-specific, clear and memorable.
MODE: HACKATHON. restrained strong cobalt blue accent #2455D6 with a localized pale blue assignment/project strip. UPCOMING EVENT says "Up next / October 12". Main composition asymmetric: left 36% with title "CivicHacks 2026" in expressive condensed bold 64px type, Hackathon tag, concise "Build practical solutions for stronger communities.", date and location, View event blue button, readable "Judging opens October 12". Right 64% dominant project spotlight with a beautiful large Voltify energy prototype screen and a narrow white text caption overlay at bottom: Voltify, Team Aurora, Energy, description. Below it a small numbered horizontal project index for Voltify / AgriSense / MedSync / LinguaLink gives tangible work. Across the next band, full width flat project list with project name, one sentence, track and a small prototype thumbnail; narrow calendar column on far right. A section "How judging works" exposes Innovation / Impact / Execution as three compact labeled criteria with short useful explanations, not score inputs. This home feels like the competition is ready for builders and judges. No decorative hero art.
